headline: Malaysian Palm Oil Futures Slip 1.1% on High Stocks and Sluggish Demand
summary: The benchmark palm oil contract on the Bursa Malaysia Derivatives Exchange slid 1.1% to 4,387 ringgit per metric ton amid high stocks, weak rival edible oils, and sluggish demand.
why: Malaysia is one of the world's largest producers and exporters of palm oil, making its benchmark futures a key indicator for the global vegetable oil market.

impacts.name: Malaysian Palm Oil
impacts.why: Accumulating domestic inventories and soft international demand weigh directly on physical palm oil contract prices.
impacts.baseline_rule: first recorded price at or after created_at (15-minute price recorder); end = first price at least 24 h later, within 48 h

why_moved: Elevated inventory levels and weakness in competing edible oil markets pressured buyers, leading to a consecutive session of price declines.
